Foyle's War

8 Series 28 Episodes Stars Michael Kitchen Hastings, 1940s Created by Anthony Horowitz

Michael Kitchen stars as Detective Chief Superintendent Christopher Foyle, a quietly principled policeman investigating crimes on the home front in Hastings during the Second World War. Created by Anthony Horowitz, Foyle's War ran for eight series and 28 feature-length episodes on ITV from 2002 to 2015, following Foyle from 1940 through the war's end and into the early Cold War. It streams on Acorn TV in the US. See how the services compare in British TV Hub's guide to where to watch British TV in the US.

New Viewer's Guide

Start Here

Series 1, The German Woman (2002)

The opening episode introduces Foyle, his driver Sam Stewart, and DS Paul Milner, and sets the tone for a series about ordinary lives tested by war. The episodes follow the war in chronological order, so watching from the beginning is the best way in.

At a Glance
Watch OrderIn order recommended
RuntimeFeature-length episodes

Best Episodes, Ranked

British TV Hub's picks, spoiler-free.

#1

The German Woman

The German-born wife of a wealthy local figure is murdered amid rising anti-German feeling, in the episode that introduces Foyle, Sam, and Milner. It establishes everything that makes the series work, from its moral seriousness to its careful sense of period.

At a Glance
PositionSeries 1, Episode 1 · 2002
Best ForFirst-time viewers
Where to WatchAcorn TV
Watch on Acorn TV →
#2

Among the Few

Sam goes undercover to find out how rationed petrol is vanishing from a fuel depot, while Foyle's RAF pilot son, Andrew, is drawn into a murder inquiry. It's a strong showcase for Sam and for the personal stakes the war brings to Foyle's own family.

At a Glance
PositionSeries 2, Episode 2 · 2003
Best ForCharacter fans
Where to WatchAcorn TV
Watch on Acorn TV →
#3

Fifty Ships

A dinner for an important American visitor becomes the backdrop to a mystery tied to Britain's efforts to win support from the United States. It blends a traditional investigation with the bigger political picture of 1940.

At a Glance
PositionSeries 2, Episode 1 · 2003
Best ForHistory lovers
Where to WatchAcorn TV
Watch on Acorn TV →
#4

The French Drop

Foyle is still hoping to contribute more directly to the war effort when a local murder places him between rival intelligence organisations. It's a tense, espionage-flavoured episode that widens the show's world.

At a Glance
PositionSeries 3, Episode 1 · 2004
Best ForEspionage fans
Where to WatchAcorn TV
Watch on Acorn TV →
#5

Invasion

American troops arrive in early 1942 to build an airstrip on a Hastings farm, and local resentment soon turns into something worse. It's a lively look at how the US presence changed life in English towns.

At a Glance
PositionSeries 4, Episode 1
Best ForHome-front history
Where to WatchAcorn TV
Watch on Acorn TV →
#6

Bleak Midwinter

The apparently accidental death of a young woman at a munitions factory becomes entangled with a case that places Milner under suspicion. It's one of the show's most personal and emotional stories, with a fittingly wintry backdrop.

At a Glance
PositionSeries 4, Episode 3
Best ForMilner fans
Where to WatchAcorn TV
Watch on Acorn TV →
#7

All Clear

In May 1945, Foyle joins a committee preparing Hastings for the Victory in Europe celebrations, only for two of its members to die. It captures the relief and unfinished business of the war's final days.

At a Glance
PositionSeries 5, Episode 3 · 2008
Best ForA satisfying wartime chapter

What Makes the Series Special

The Home Front

Rationing, Real Wartime Issues

Each episode builds its mystery around a real aspect of wartime life, from internment and the black market to rationing and conscientious objectors, so the history is as absorbing as the whodunit.

At a Glance
FocusWartime Britain
Period1940–1947
Lead Performance

Understated Integrity

Michael Kitchen plays Foyle with remarkable restraint, letting a pause or a glance do the work, and the result is one of British television's most quietly commanding detectives.

At a Glance
StyleRestrained, principled
Fan Favourite

Brought Back by Viewers

ITV cancelled the series after Series 5 in 2007, then revived it following strong ratings and viewer support, and it continued into the post-war years until 2015.

At a Glance
CancelledAfter Series 5
RevivedRan to 2015

Setting and Filming Locations

Setting & Filming

Wartime Hastings, Then Post-War London

Series 1 to 6 are set in and around Hastings on the Sussex coast from 1940 to the end of the war, and the town itself was used for filming. Series 7 and 8 move to post-war London, where Foyle works for British intelligence in the early Cold War, with some Series 7 filming taking place in Ireland.

At a Glance
TownHastings, Sussex
Later SeriesPost-war London

Frequently Asked Questions

Status

Is Foyle's War finished?

Yes. Foyle's War ended in 2015 after eight series and 28 episodes.

Quick Answer
StatusComplete
Ended2015
Streaming

Where can I watch Foyle's War in the US?

Foyle's War streams on Acorn TV in the US, including through the Acorn TV channel on Amazon Prime Video. Selected episodes may also appear through participating PBS stations.

Quick Answer
PrimaryAcorn TV
Viewing Order

Do I need to watch Foyle's War in order?

It's recommended. Each episode is a self-contained mystery, but the series follows the war chronologically and the characters' lives develop from episode to episode.

Quick Answer
In Order?Recommended
Source

Is Foyle's War based on a book?

No. Foyle's War is an original series created and largely written by Anthony Horowitz, who is also the author of the Magpie Murders novels.

Quick Answer
SourceOriginal series
CreatorAnthony Horowitz
Setting

Why does Foyle's War leave Hastings?

Once the war ended, the final two series moved Foyle to London and into the world of British intelligence, exploring the early years of the Cold War.

Quick Answer
Series 7–8Post-war London
Filming Location

Where was Foyle's War filmed?

Much of the wartime series was filmed in Hastings itself, which is also where the story is set.

Quick Answer
TownHastings
